title: NDJSON tool-fallback compatibility harness and backpressure regression
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a focused regression harness that validates newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) structured outputs across streaming + tool/function calling codepaths, with special attention to backpressure scenarios, incremental parse fidelity, and graceful tool fallback. The goal is to catch regressions where partial/fragmented JSON events or toolcall messages could cause downstream consumers (SDKs, Console parsers, or third-party integrators) to mis-parse or deadlock. This ticket covers test corpus, golden-ndjson fixtures, CI integration, and flaky-test hardening for the harness.
acceptance_criteria: The harness can replay 50+ golden NDJSON scenarios (including interleaved tokens, half-chunk JSON fragments, and toolcall boundary conditions) against all supported streaming endpoints.
CI jobs run the harness on each runtime change and fail the build on deterministic parse regressions; transient failures are retried with instrumentation captured.

When the runtime triggers a tool fallback (secondary model/variant), the NDJSON stream preserves message boundaries and tooling metadata (request_id, seq, is_final) in >99.9% of samples in the golden suite.
SDKs (JS/Python) and Console parsers can consume streams from the harness without needing custom shim code — documented discrepancies are captured as issues.
Test artifacts (golden inputs + expected parsed event sequences) are stored in Drive and referenced by fixtures in the repo; a reproducible local runner is available for engineers.
A follow-up triage playbook is added for flaky or non-deterministic failures with links to dashboards and recommended mitigations.
test_plan: Assemble a golden-corpus of NDJSON edgecases: trailing commas, escaped newlines, split braces across chunks, nested function-call payloads, and mixed binary payload markers.
Write a harness that can drive streaming endpoints at multiple chunk sizes and simulated network delays to reproduce backpressure and fragment boundaries.
Add toolcall scenarios where the model emits a tool invocation mid-object; validate the parser either yields a complete tool event or buffers until full event is received.
Integrate harness as a matrix job in CI: runtime variants (cpu/gpu/quantized), sequence lengths, and backpressure profiles.
Create a smoke canary that runs on each model rollout; failures create an automated alert and create a Linear issue with log bundle attached.
Coordinate with SDK owners to run their parsers against the harness and collect incompatibility reports.
updates: 2025-01-08: Ticket created during compatibility sprint planning. Identified NDJSON as recurring source of SDK parsing bugs.
2025-01-15: Collected initial golden samples from production bug triage and Console logs (11 unique failure patterns).
2025-01-22: Prototype harness implemented; can replay samples locally with simulated chunk sizes. Observed two failure modes: premature event close and toolcall metadata loss.
2025-01-30: Added CI integration draft (pipeline branch) and a retry wrapper for flaky network simulations. Opened PR #5123 for review.
2025-02-10: SDK owners (Python/JS) validated harness against their parsers; documented 3 parser assumptions that need alignment (seq numbering, is_final semantics, and early-EOF behavior).
2025-02-15: Hardening iteration complete: added detailed instrumentation (byte offsets, chunk boundaries) to aid debugging; ticket moved to In Progress for GL review and wider rollout planning.
notes: This harness emphasizes observable instrumentation (byte offsets, sequence ids) so that when a failure is detected we can reliably attribute whether it was a kernel-level prefetch issue, an SDK parser bug, or a protocol-layer regression. We will iterate the golden set based on new production failures and keep the CI job in a non-blocking mode for two weeks before switching to blocking to minimize developer disruption.
